note: Every file under orcel_agent/ copied or adapted from DeerFlow is listed here with its source path, source blob, destination, decision (COPY or ADAPT) and modifications, and names its DeerFlow path and the pin in a header. Slice 1 imports no donor code.

modifications: Copied unchanged in logic: argument normalisation, the read-range window, the per-tool call key, the order-independent call-set hash, both detection layers (identical call sets; windowed per-tool frequency with decay and re-arming), warn-once, the decision record, and the warning queue (deduplicated, newest four kept, merged deduplicated into one 'loop_warning' message, restored when a model call fails).

Tool names mapped to the Orcel edge: read_file -> fs_read / fs_read_range (max_lines, defaulting to the edge's 200, becomes the end line; workspace_id joins the read key); write_file / str_replace -> fs_write / fs_edit; bash / ls / glob / grep -> fs_list / fs_find / fs_search (no description argument on the Orcel fs tools, so the narration rule is kept only for faithfulness).
One detector per agent run: LangGraph runtime, thread/run scoping, LRU eviction, fallback run ids and the lock removed.
AgentMiddleware hooks replaced by ChatModelPlanner calling track() and drain_warnings(); a hard stop becomes a Finish with stop_reason loop_capped.
Wrap-up text no longer asks the agent to write files (the agent is read-only).
Decisions go to the agent's EventLog instead of DeerFlow's audit context and run-event catalogue; logging removed.
Per-tool frequency defaults scaled to the agent's 32-step budget: warn 12, stop 20 (DeerFlow 30, 50, which could never fire within it). Identical-call defaults unchanged (3, 5, window 20).

The hard-stop answer appends the stop message to the reply's text (DeerFlow's _append_text, reduced to the plain-text answer a Finish carries); the stop reason travels in Finish.stop_reason and RunResult.stop_reason instead of consume_stop_reason().
Uses DeerFlow's deterministic head/tail tool-output sampling design and model-side budgeting, without importing its LangGraph middleware, tool dispatcher, storage or sandbox.
Builds a local bounded JSON structural hint (counts only) with no file reference and no externalized output; no data or tool result is written to disk.
The original output remains with the in-process Step, while only the model-bound ToolMessage gets a strict 16000-character preview (including metadata).
Rejects invalid caller budgets, always marks an oversized preview as untrusted and not an execution receipt, and uses a SHA-256 prefix for stable diagnostics.
